previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with nausea, vomiting, black stools, and fevers. She has chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) on Gleevec. Workup revealed progression to blast crisis, confirmed by bone marrow biopsy showing 16% blasts. Initial treatment with HyperCVAD and dasatinib was switched to 7+3 induction after immunophenotyping confirmed myeloblastic crisis. The hospital course was complicated by neutropenic fever, and blood cultures grew Leptotrichia trevosani, leading to broad-spectrum antibiotics and replacement of her Hickman line with a PICC. She developed severe nausea and vomiting, resulting in a Mallory-Weiss tear confirmed by endoscopy. Her nausea was controlled with PPI, Zofran, and Zyprexa. She also had pneumonia and sinusitis, both managed supportively. Repeat bone marrow biopsies showed decreasing blasts, with no clear population detected by day 49. She improved clinically, became afebrile, and her counts recovered. She was discharged home on oral metronidazole for 9 days, with plans to restart dasatinib and proceed to transplant evaluation.

radiology_notes.text:
DIAGNOSIS: ___ y/o woman with CML admitted for BMT.

PROCEDURE:  Temporary central venous catheter placement, right side.

INDICATION:  IV access, chemotherapy.

PHYSICIANS:  Dr. ___ Dr. ___.  Dr. ___ was the attending
physician who supervised the entire procedure.

COMPLICATIONS:  None.

TECHNIQUE AND FINDINGS:  After the risks, benefits, and alternatives of the
proposed procedure as well as those of conscious sedation were thoroughly
explained to the patient, informed consent was obtained.  Patient was taken to
the angiography suite and placed in supine position.  The right neck was
prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A pre-procedure timeout was
performed.  Next, ultrasound guidance was used to accessing the right external
jugular vein with a micropuncture needle.  Hard copy images were obtained for
the medical record.  Of note, the internal jugular vein was diminutive
possibly related to prior instrumentation.

A 0.018 nitinol wire was then passed through the needle and into the SVC.  A
skin ___ was made over the needle, which was then removed.  A micropuncture
sheath was then placed over the wire.  After appropriate length measurements
were made, the wire and introducer were then removed.  A ___ wire was then
passed through the sheath and into the IVC.  Next, a triple-lumen ___
central venous catheter was positioned over the wire with the tip at the level
of the SVC using fluoroscopic guidance.  The wire was then removed, where
three ports were aspirated and flushed.  A 0 silk suture was used x 2 to
secure the catheter in place. Sterile dressing was applied.  The patient
tolerated the procedure well without immediate complication.

IMPRESSION:

Uncomplicated placement of right-sided temporary triple-lumen central venous
line via the right external jugular vein.  The catheter tip is in the SVC and
the catheter is ready to use.

PROCEDURE:  Left tunneled triple-lumen central venous catheter.

INDICATION:  Chemotherapy.

COMPLICATIONS:  None.

ANESTHESIA:  Local anesthesia was established of approximately 15 cc of 1%
lidocaine.

PHYSICIANS:  Drs. ___.  Dr. ___ was the attending physician
who reviewed the procedure.

TECHNIQUE AND FINDINGS:  After the risks, benefits, and alternatives of the
proposed procedure as well as those of conscious sedation were thoroughly
explained to the patient, informed consent was obtained.  Patient was taken to
the angiography suite and placed in supine position.  The left neck was
prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A pre-procedure timeout was
performed.  Next, a micropuncture needle was used to access the left internal
jugular vein under ultrasound guidance.  Hard copy images were obtained for
the medical record.  A 0.018 wire was passed through the needle and into the
SVC.  A skin ___ was made over the needle, which was then removed.  A
micropuncture sheath was then placed over the wire.  After appropriate length
measurements were made, the wire and inner introducer were removed.  A ___
wire was then passed through the sheath and into the IVC.  Next, the skin
along the proposed tract site was anesthetized using 1% lidocaine with
epinephrine.  A skin ___ was made approximately two fingerbreadths beneath
the left clavicle and the catheter cut to appropriate length was then brought
through the incision and out of the puncture site with a tunneling device.  A
peelaway sheath was then placed over the wire and the wire and introducer were
then removed.  The catheter was placed through the peelaway sheath and
positioned with the tip at the level of the inferior SVC using fluoroscopic
guidance. The peelaway sheath was then removed.  The ports were aspirated and
flushed. ___ Vicryl was used to close the puncture site.  A 0 silk suture was
used to secure the catheter in place.  Sterile dressing was applied.  The
patient tolerated the procedure well without immediate complication.

IMPRESSION:

Uncomplicated placement of triple-lumen ___ tunneled catheter via the left
internal jugular vein.  The tip is in the SVC and the catheter is ready to
use.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Followup of a patient in CML with blast crisis before
stem cell transplantation.

PROCEDURE:  Using sterile technique, the cuff of the catheter was exposed from

A sterile dressing was applied.

PORTABLE CHEST ___

INDICATION:  PICC placement.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  New left PICC terminates in the lower SVC near the junction with
the right atrium.  Pre-existing right internal jugular catheter is unchanged
in position, and a previous left-sided central venous catheter has been
removed with no evidence of pneumothorax.  Cardiac silhouette is mildly
enlarged, and lungs are clear.

INDICATIONS:  ___ woman with recent stem cell transplant for acute
myelogenous leukemia, with febrile neutropenia and upper and lower abdominal
pain.

COMPARISONS:  The chest can be compared to ___, the abdomen to a CT torso
from ___ and a more recent MR from ___, to some extent.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial CT images of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis were obtained
without oral or intravenous contrast.  Intravenous contrast was not given at
the request of the referring physician.  The patient declined oral contrast.
Sagittal and coronal reformations were performed.

FINDINGS:  There is a PICC line which terminates in the right ventricle.  A
right internal central jugular venous catheter terminates at the cavoatrial
junction in a suitable position.  Small calcified left hilar lymph nodes are
unchanged.  Coronary artery calcifications are again present with a minimal
pericardial effusion, but less than before.  No pleural effusions are present.
There is a patchy residual ground-glass opacity, mostly peribronchovascular in
distribution, including residual ___ opacities in the right upper
lobe.  However, the appearance is much improved and appears most compatible
with resolving pneumonia, without an evidence for a new process. In the
periphery of the right upper lobe, there is again a calcified granuloma with
adjacent subpleural scarring, unchanged in extent.  Elsewhere, the lungs are
clear.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  There are a few calcifications in the
spleen and one tiny one in the liver, suggestive of an old granulomatous
process.  The patient is status post cholecystectomy.  There is no biliary
dilatation.  The pancreas and adrenal glands are within normal limits.  The
kidneys are unremarkable.  Within the limitations of lack of opacification of
the bowel, no definite abnormality is demonstrated.  A few sigmoid diverticula
are present, but without diverticulitis.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  The uterus, rectum, and bladder are
unremarkable.  There is no lymphadenopathy.

BONE WINDOWS:  There are no suspicious focal lesions.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Persistent patchy opacities in the right upper lobe suggestive of
resolving pneumonia.  No evidence for new infectious process compared to the
exam from one month ago.

2.  No definite cause for fever identified.

3.  PICC line terminating in the right ventricle.  Repositioning of the
malpositioned-catheter is recommended.

Findings and recommendations discussed with Dr. ___ on the same day.

REASON FOR EXAM:  PICC.

Since ___ chest x-ray and ___ CT torso, the left PICC tip
was pulled back, now ending in the cavoatrial junction near the right atrium. 
Right internal jugular catheter still ends in the low SVC.  Right mid lung
opacities are better depicted by the recent CT torso.  Lungs are otherwise
clear.  There is no pleural effusion.  Clips of cholecystectomy present.  The
cardiomediastinal silhouette and hilar contours are normal.

HISTORY:  ___ female with CML status post allotransplant, now with
right upper quadrant pain and fevers.

COMPARISON:  CT, ___.

FINDINGS:  The hepatic echotexture is normal, without a focal lesion.  The
patient is status post cholecystectomy, without any abnormality identified
within the gallbladder fossa.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary
ductal dilatation with the CBD measuring 3 mm.  The portal vein is patent with
hepatopetal flow.  The spleen is normal in size.  Visualized pancreatic head
is unremarkable, with the remainder of the pancreas not well visualized due to
overlying bowel gas.

IMPRESSION:  Normal hepatic echotexture, without evidence of a focal lesion.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with CML and fevers and elevated LFTs.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the torso.  No
contrast was administered.  Multiplanar reformatted images were generated.

CT CHEST WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  A left PICC terminates in the right atrium. The
heart size is stable with a physiologic amount of fluid in the pericardial
space.  Coronary artery calcifications are again noted.  There is no hilar or
mediastinal lymphadenopathy by size criteria.  A precarinal lymph node
measures 9 mm, stable.  There is no axillary lymphadenopathy by size criteria.

Within the lungs, foci of ground-glass opacity and peribronchovascular nodules
in the right upper lobe anteriorly and the right lower lobe posteriorly are
stable, again consistent with infectious etiology.  There is no new
consolidation or pleural effusion.  The tracheobronchial tree remains patent
to subsegmental levels.  Calcified granuloma is noted in the anterior right
upper lobe.  Hilar calcifications are also noted.

CT ABDOMEN WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  The patient is post-cholecystectomy with
clips in the gallbladder fossa. Additionally, there is a clip posterior to the
liver.  In the absence of IV contrast, evaluation of solid organs is limited.
However, the liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands, kidneys, stomach and
duodenum are unremarkable.  The spleen demonstrates calcified granuloma along
its upper pole, unchanged and is otherwise unremarkable.  There is no
hydronephrosis or renal stone.  There is no free air or free fluid in the
abdomen.  There is no mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy by size
criteria.

CT PELVIS WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  There is a small amount of simple fluid in the
pelvis, new since the prior study.  However, loops of large and small bowel
are stable, with scattered diverticulosis of the sigmoid colon but no evidence
of diverticulitis.  The appendix is normal.  The large and small bowel is
otherwise unremarkable.  The urinary bladder, distal ureters, uterus and
adnexa are within normal limits.  There is no pelvic or inguinal
lymphadenopathy by size criteria.  A surgical clip is noted in the omental fat
anterior to a loop of small bowel in the pelvic midline, without associated
inflammatory changes.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There is no fracture or worrisome bony lesion. Multilevel
degenerative changes are noted at the spine.  Soft tissues demonstrate
calcified focus in the subcutaneous tissues of the left buttock, likely
related to injection.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No new abnormalities in the torso to explain symptoms.
2.  Stable patchy opacities in the right upper lobe and right lower lobe,
unchanged, consistent with prior infection.  No findings to suggest new
infection.
3.  Diverticulosis without diverticulitis.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with left PICC line placement.

___. 

AP UPRIGHT CHEST:  A left PICC terminates in the low SVC.  The right internal
jugular catheter has been removed.   The cardiomediastinal silhouette is
unremarkable.  The lungs are clear without effusion, consolidation, or
pneumothorax. Right upper abdominal clips are stable. 

IMPRESSION:  Left PICC terminates in the low SVC.  There is no acute
cardiopulmonary process.
